title: Northreach renewal + EU on-prem capacity & retainer sync
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on bumping dedicated capacity, a small EU on-prem pilot for data residency, and contract retainer extension. Customer asked for detailed pricing tiers for dedicated pools vs burst, SOC2 / KMS controls, and an on-prem timeline. Agreed to a technical workshop and a pilot SOW draft by next week.
action_items: Samir: Prepare sizing spreadsheet for 2x/3x capacity scenarios and cost delta by 2026-06-23
Jordan: Send draft SOW for EU on-prem pilot and retainer amendment by 2026-06-25
Ava: Share SOC2 report, network diagram, and KMS integration notes by 2026-06-22
Daniel: Provide current QPS and peak 95th percentile token counts by 2026-06-21
next_steps: Schedule technical workshop (deep dive on on-prem packaging and deployment) — propose Tue/Wed next week
Share detailed pricing (dedicated pools, burst credits, on-prem pilot cost) and draft SOW
Run a 2-week pilot with a single EU on-prem node and canary traffic routing
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-18 15:00 UTC, Duration ~38m. Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood CSM), Marta (Northreach MLOps), Daniel (Northreach Platform), Priya (CISO), Ethan (Procurement).

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to use this slot to walk through renewal options and the eu on-prem pilot ask, should be about 30ish minutes then q&a.
00:22 Marta: thanks, yeah we got your note — we're coming up on the end of the retainer and traffic has been steady up, we've got some new customers in the eu so data residency is now a blocker.
00:35 Samir: cool, can you share a bit about current baseline? qps, token profile, peak windows? even rough percentiles help.
00:48 Daniel: sure, current is about 350 qps average for chat endpoints, token size average ~420, 95th peaks around 1,200 qps for short bursts, monthly tokens around 60M. sorry i might have chopped that, we can send the spreadsheet.
01:05 Samir: that helps — so right now you're on Redwood Hosted with a reserved retainer, correct?
01:11 Marta: yes, we've got a small dedicated pool for critical routes plus hosted fallback. the thing is latency for eu customers is creeping up and our legal team wants eu on-prem for PII processing.
01:25 Priya: to emphasize, compliance is the driver here. SOC2 is table stakes, and KMS-backed encryption for both at-rest and in-transit keys. we also need SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC.
01:40 Ava: absolutely, we support SSO/SAML and RBAC for console and API keys, and we have KMS integrations — i'll put the SOC2 and KMS notes in the follow-up.
01:52 Jordan: high level options: 1) expand Dedicated capacity in eu region (hosted by redwood but isolated pool), 2) EU on-prem pilot — private deployment inside your network (V-P-C / VPC) with a customer-controlled KMS, 3) hybrid: keep control plane hosted with private data plane. each has cost/ops tradeoffs.
02:11 Ethan: procurement cares about predictability. is there a monthly commit for dedicated vs a one-time on-prem license + retainer?
02:21 Jordan: dedicated is commit-based monthly; on-prem is a platform license + support + optional dedicated node reserves. i'll detail numbers in the pricing attachment.
02:32 Samir: technical nuance — on-prem means we ship a private control plane package and the inference nodes, it's not totally air-gapped unless you require. KV cache and prefix caching works the same but we do need to validate kernel/quantization profiles on your hardware.
02:50 Daniel: question: our infra is mixed — we have bare metal in eu and some k8s clusters; do you support both?
03:00 Samir: yes, the private package supports k8s and a bare-metal agent. we may need to run a short compatibility test, especially around GPU types and CUDA/mkl versions, and there can be slight perf deltas — we'll run a benchmarking pass.
03:18 Marta: timeline-wise, we need something in eu for Q4 launch. what is a realistic pilot timeline?
03:25 Samir: typical pilot is 2–4 weeks for install and validation, then a 2-week canary with limited traffic. so start-to-first-traffic could be 3–6 weeks depending on approvals.
03:36 Priya: what about audit logs and tamper-evidence for the on-prem setup? someone from legal may ask for chain of custody.
03:44 Ava: our private offering includes audit logs shipped to your central SIEM or stored locally; we can enable immutable logs and a retention policy. i'll add the audit log architecture diagram.
03:57 Daniel: any differences in failover? if the on-prem node goes down, can traffic route to hosted as fallback?
04:05 Samir: yes, we support automatic fallback to hosted variants; that's a common pattern for hybrid deployments. the routing policy is configurable per-route with a canary/fallback window.
04:18 Marta: cost question — how does dedicated vs on-prem compare per token?
04:25 Jordan: rough rule: dedicated hosted tends to be cheaper per-token for steady state because we manage infra and multi-tenant efficiencies. on-prem has higher up-front and ops costs but satisfies residency and some compliance needs. we'll quantify in the pricing.
04:38 Ethan: procurement needs an MSA amendment and a SOW for the pilot, also invoice terms — net30 is fine but we might ask for net45 given internal approvals.
04:49 Jordan: we can do net45 for the pilot; for long-term commits we'll follow standard contract process. i'll loop in legal.
04:58 Marta: one more — competitor question, our infra team flagged BigCloudAI because they offered a managed eu endpoint; why pick Redwood?
05:06 Samir: two reasons — production-grade runtime comparators (we've seen lower tail latency given our batching + KV caching) and the unified operations model across hosted/dedicated/private which reduces friction when moving between modes. also our Optimize tooling helps reduce token spend.
05:28 Daniel: small nit — last benchmark i saw the memory footprint differed between quantization modes, is there a recommended profile for our 48GB A100s?
05:37 Samir: we'll recommend a quantization profile after we run the compatibility pass; for 48GB A100s we typically do q4_0 or a mixed int8 path, but depends on model architecture and perf/quality tradeoffs.
05:54 Marta: ok sounds good. can we recap actions?
06:00 Jordan: recap: Samir runs sizing + benchmark plan; Jordan sends pricing and draft SOW; Ava shares security pack; Daniel provides traffic numbers; procurement will review terms and confirm net45 or ask for exceptions.
06:18 Priya: expect legal to ask for SOC2 artifact and encryption attestation.
06:25 Ava: noted, i'll attach SOC2 and an architecture diagram.
06:32 Ethan: we'll try to get procurement sign-off by end of month but can't promise, procurement cycles are a bit slow.
06:41 Jordan: totally fine — next steps: propose two slots for a 90-minute technical workshop next week (deep dive on on-prem), i'll ping calendar.
06:52 Marta: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
07:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard acronyms (V-P-C noted), some token counts rounded, proper nouns may be slightly off.
